# harness-quarters

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
Links each agent harness's home to its instructions, skills, settings and hooks, for the
person running agents across these hosts. It keeps model picks and trust out of git,
records what each harness has been shown to do, pins pi and relay, and archives sessions.
The instruction corpus and profiles live in lore; the flow system lives in flows.

Authority: `docs/specs/2026-10-06-residue-design.md`
<!-- ops:identity end -->

This is one person's working configuration for coding agents, published as a reference
rather than as a package. It is wired to its owner's other projects and hosts, so a
clone does not run as-is. Its examples cover declared home links, harness settings,
session-state filters and transcript archives. The instruction corpus, profiles and
general skill collection live in lore; hq delivers them through its link manifest.

## Setup

Once per clone:

    just setup

It points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`, registers the `harness-state` filter, and
creates `local/codex/rules/`. `local/` is untracked (see Layout). The work configs
under it come from another host's `local/`, never from `just setup`. The repository's git
config, these filter keys included, lives in the checkout's `.git`, which syncs between
hosts with the rest of the checkout, so one host's `just setup` reaches the others. A
host still runs `just setup` once after pulling a change to the recipe: it is
idempotent, and it does not rely on the synced config or `local/` having arrived.

The filter is three keys of git config. `filter.harness-state.clean` runs
`.githooks/harness-state-clean %f`. `filter.harness-state.required = true` makes a
failing clean stop the git command (`git add`, `git diff`, `git status` on a changed
config) instead of staging the live file unfiltered. `filter.harness-state.smudge = cat`
is the identity: git treats a required filter with no smudge as failed at every
checkout of a filtered file, so the smudge must be set, and it changes nothing. The
hooks check all three: `harness-state-refresh` and the pre-commit hook refuse, naming
`just setup`, when any differs. Hooks older than `harnesses.toml` neither need nor check
the two newer keys; backing them out, only to roll back to such hooks, unsets both:
`git config --unset filter.harness-state.required && git config --unset filter.harness-state.smudge`.

`harnesses.toml` declares, for each tracked live config, the path glob the filter takes
(`.gitattributes` routes exactly those globs to it, and nothing else), the keys and
tables it strips, and the pick units `live-picks` saves. The filter keeps `model`,
`modelSettings` and `effortLevel` in `harnesses/claude/settings*.json`,
the top-level `model` and `model_reasoning_effort` in `harnesses/codex/config*.toml`,
`defaultProvider`, `defaultModel` and `defaultThinkingLevel` in `harnesses/pi/settings*.json`
(with pi's installation ids, `deviceId` and `trackingId`), and `model`, `effort`,
`effortByBase`, `trustedWorkspaces` and `seasonalThemesOptIn` in `harnesses/agy/settings*.json` out
of the index: model and effort picks (and agy's trusted workspace list and seasonal theme
opt-in) write into the live files (the homes symlink here), and they are session or host
state, not configuration. agy's other settings-UI writes are configuration and are
tracked, `showFeedbackSurvey` and `statusLine` included. A fresh home
therefore runs each harness's default model and effort until the first pick.

While `harnesses.toml` is broken (bad TOML, or an entry its validation refuses), the
filter fails, and so does every git command that runs it on a changed config: nothing
unfiltered is staged. Restore the manifest (`git checkout -- harnesses.toml`, or fix
it); never unset `filter.harness-state.required` to get past it. The same refusal
follows a live config that is not valid JSON (a trailing comma, JSONC) or a
`.githooks/harness_state.py` that will not import: the filter prints
`harness-state-clean: <path>: <problem>` (or `cannot load .githooks/harness_state.py`)
and git stops; fix the file or restore the module. During a merge or rebase,
`git checkout -- harnesses.toml` fails on an unmerged path: resolve the conflict, or run
`git merge --abort` / `git rebase --abort`, instead. A config blob staged
while the filter was not configured (before `just setup`, or across a checkout of a
commit older than the manifest) keeps the picks it was staged with; the pre-commit hook
refuses it until `git add --renormalize <path>` stages it through the filter.

The working tree keeps the harness's last pick, and a checkout of the file drops it.
`.githooks/live-picks` puts it back. At every turn end it saves the picks from
`harnesses/claude/settings.json` and `harnesses/codex/config.toml` in local/live-picks.json,
`harnesses/pi/settings.json` in the separate local/live-picks-pi.json record, and
`harnesses/agy/settings.json` in local/live-picks-agy.json. The
`post-checkout`, `post-merge` and `post-rewrite` hooks restore it right after a git
command drops it, in the main checkout only, and the next turn end restores it where
no hook runs (the commands listed below for trust). Each picker's fields are one unit:
Claude's `/model` (`model`, `modelSettings`) and `/effort` (`effortLevel`) separately,
Codex's model and effort together; pi's default model (`defaultProvider`,
`defaultModel`) and thinking level (`defaultThinkingLevel`) separately; agy's `/model`
(`model`), `/effort` (`effort`, `effortByBase`), workspace trust
(`trustedWorkspaces`) and the seasonal theme opt-in (`seasonalThemesOptIn`) separately. A unit holding
any of its fields is never touched, so a newer pick always wins, and a pick of one
Claude, pi or agy picker keeps the other's saved value. A unit holding none is ambiguous,
so only an explicit act resets the saved pick:
`.githooks/live-picks forget harnesses/claude/settings.json` (or `harnesses/codex/config.toml`,
`harnesses/pi/settings.json` or `harnesses/agy/settings.json`), which resets every unit of that file and
removes them from it.
Claude's `/model` Default clears its fields and the next turn end may
restore the saved pick; use `forget` for a deliberate reset. PostModelSwitch fires
before the settings write and may skip a reset to the same resolved model, so it is
not a capture point. The tested Codex picker actions kept both model fields; use
`forget` to return it to its default. Because agy saves `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`
by atomic rename over the home link, an anchored host (one whose `~/.gemini/config`
hooks or skills link already targets this checkout) reads any regular file there during
`capture`, adopts its picks and any tracked `/config` or `permissions` edits back into
`harnesses/agy/settings.json`, and restores the symlink on `restore`, `hook` and `forget` (a host
not anchored yet adopts a first-run file through `just link --apply` instead; see Home
links). A
Claude or Codex pick made since the last turn end is not saved yet; a git command in
that window brings back the one before (for agy, `hook` captures a detached regular file
before restoring onto the newly checked-out `harnesses/agy/settings.json`).

The pi extension `harnesses/pi/extensions/harness-state.ts` calls the same refresh after `model_select` and
`thinking_level_select` (yielding for the settings write), at `agent_settled` and at
`session_shutdown`. Setting the current model or thinking level as the default can
emit no event: that default is saved at the next turn end or exit. A Git rewrite in
that window restores the previous saved default; set it again or use
`.githooks/live-picks forget harnesses/pi/settings.json` to reset both units to the automatic
default. Runs are serialised, with a 10-second limit followed by one second for
process-group termination. Picker and turn-end handlers return without waiting;
shutdown awaits the current run and one final run, delaying exit by at most about
22 seconds. If pi exits without running shutdown handlers, a synchronous exit handler
kills any refresh group it still owns. A failure warns once per session without
failing the pi operation.

Each record is machine-owned: an invalid record is refused independently, never
overwritten, and deleting it starts that record over. pi's and agy's separate records let the
previous tool keep saving Claude and Codex picks during recovery. To back the extension
out, revert its merge, remove the `~/.pi/agent/extensions/harness-state.ts` link on each
host and run `just link-check`.
The previous tool ignores local/live-picks-pi.json and local/live-picks-agy.json, which may be deleted; Claude and
Codex preservation continues. pi then keeps defaults only until a Git rewrite drops
them.

Codex's project trust, the
`[projects."<path>"]` tables it adds to `harnesses/codex/config*.toml`, is host state and stays
out of the index the same way. So any git command that writes a new blob of
`harnesses/codex/config.toml` over the live file drops the whole list, on every host at once,
since the checkout is shared through Dropbox. `.githooks/codex-trust` puts it back. At
every turn end the Stop hook below saves the live tables into
local/codex/trust.toml, never removing one, and inserts the ones the live file lacks
before its first table header. The `post-checkout`, `post-merge` and `post-rewrite`
hooks insert them right after a switch, a checkout of the file, a merge or a rebase,
in the main checkout only. A hook that fails reports on stderr and exits 0, so a
switch that worked does not exit 1; the next turn end retries. Where no hook runs
(`git stash`, `git reset --hard`, `git cherry-pick`, `git revert`, `git rebase --abort`,
`git merge --abort`, a merge stopped on a conflict, a rebase that only fast-forwards, a
fresh clone that has a saved copy), the list is back at the next turn end. A Codex session started before
then asks again. While the main checkout is on a branch older than these hooks,
nothing restores the list until the checkout switches back. A table Codex added since
the last turn end is not saved yet. local/codex/trust.toml is machine-owned: capture rewrites it whole, so a comment
added by hand is lost. Restoring also takes group and other access off the live
`harnesses/codex/config.toml`, which a checkout rewrites with the umask's mode. Nothing prunes the
saved copy: to forget a directory, run `.githooks/codex-trust forget <path>`, which
deletes its table from both files.

Since the local layer kept trust out of the index (2026-09,
`docs/specs/2026-09-28-local-layer-design.md`), worktrees and branches made
before it show `harnesses/codex/config*.toml` as modified, because their blobs still carry
trust tables, and a rebase there can stop on them.
`git checkout -- harnesses/codex/config.toml` in a worktree is safe, since worktree copies
are not live. It drops Codex's bookkeeping the same way:
`screen_reader_detection_done` under `[tui]`, the whole
`[tui.model_availability_nux]` table, and `last_updated` / `last_revision` under
each `[marketplaces.*]` table, so a fresh clone probes once and refetches its
marketplaces. Everything else the harness writes — plugin toggles, marketplace
sources, hook trust hashes — is tracked as usual.

One residual: git decides "modified" from the file's size before it runs the
filter, so a switch whose value changes length leaves the file marked `M` in
`git status` (and `git diff-index`) until the next `git add` of it — `git diff`
is content-true. A Stop hook in Claude, Codex and agy (`.githooks/harness-state-refresh`,
wired in `harnesses/claude/settings*.json`, `harnesses/codex/hooks*.json` and `harnesses/agy/hooks.json` through the
`~/.local/bin` link in `links.toml`) stages each harness config
whose filtered diff is empty, so the mark clears at the end of the turn that made
it; pi's extension calls the same refresh at the events above. It skips while another
git process holds the index lock. By hand, `git add -u -- claude codex pi agy` does the same
while staging only real changes. Do not `git stash` these files to get past it: the stash tree
equals `HEAD`, so `stash pop` brings back the file without its model pick until the next turn end restores it.
Their tests run with `just test`.

The pre-commit hook refuses any staged path under `local/`, which only `git add -f`
can stage. Lore checks the generated Projects block in its global instructions,
including the staged copy at commit time. Change the owning project's
`identity.toml` (or its table in ops's identity mirror, until it adopts), then run
just projects in ops to refresh its owned fragment, then just assemble in lore
to regenerate the delivered instructions and provenance manifest.

Right after the local/ refusal the hook runs `tools/ops-check`, vendored from ops: the
hygiene checks ops projects share (guide references, conflicted copies, agent scratch,
machine layout and adopted copies). It reads the tracked files in the working tree, not
the staged blobs, so a finding in any tracked file refuses every commit, record commits
from `tasks` included, until it is fixed, and a crash or a malformed `.ops-check.toml`
refuses too. A new attachment that carries host values (a hostname, the home directory,
WORK_ROOT, a registered checkout or its parent directory) follows the attachment
fallback in lore `skills/references/retained-item-records.md`: the raw bytes stay under
WORK_ROOT, owned by a task, and a portable derivative is attached. `.ops-check.toml` is
never widened for an attachment. Thirteen pre-commit tests cover the local-layer
refusal, the hygiene check, the guide check and the filter config from a linked
worktree; `just test` runs them.

The same hook runs `tools/ops-docs check`, vendored from ops: the identity regions at
the top of this file and of `AGENTS.md` are generated from `identity.toml`, and
`just docs` regenerates them.

Last, the hook exports the tree the commit will hold and runs two staged checkers over
it: `tools/harness-facts check` (below) and `.githooks/harness_state.py check
--staged-tree`. The second validates `harnesses.toml` and `.gitattributes` as staged,
refuses a staged config blob holding anything the filter strips (naming
`git add --renormalize <path>`), and reads the filter config from the repository's own
git config, which a linked worktree shares, so a commit from a worktree is held to the
same three keys. A staged deletion of `harnesses.toml` or of the checker is refused.

## Usage

Things you can take from here without the rest:

- `agents/skills/session-logs/` and `agents/bin/session-episodes`: read local harness
  session stores and turn transcripts into evidence. The remaining agent tools,
  including `agents/bin/wake-judge`, stay here.
- Global instructions live in lore `instructions/AGENTS.md`; profile fragments
  live in lore `profiles/`. General skills and their references live in lore,
  including its pinned superpowers submodule. The manifest links each skill to its
  owner: lore, flows, [tasks](https://github.com/khughitt/tasks), ops, or hq's
  session-logs skill.
- `.githooks/harness-state-clean` with `.githooks/harness_state.py` and
  `harnesses.toml`: a git clean filter that keeps `/model` and `/effort` picks, Codex
  bookkeeping and Codex/agy project trust out of committed harness configs. It cleans a
  path only when one `filter_glob` in `harnesses.toml` matches it and refuses any other
  path, JSON or TOML, so a reuse elsewhere declares its configs there and in
  `.gitattributes`, and sets the three filter keys `just setup` sets.
- `tools/harness-links` with `links.toml`: declares every link from a harness home into a
  checkout. Targets are checkout-relative or `<project>:<relative-path>`, resolved
  through `tasks projects --paths`. `[directories]` declares real directories, with
  each value naming the former link target that may be converted; `[retired]` names
  links to remove only while their targets still match. `just link` reports,
  `just link --apply` converges, and `just link-check` fails on drift. A foreign
  directory link or retired path is refused; undeclared paths are left alone.
  Converting the declared `~/.agents` directory happens before installing its child
  links. The directories are real; their child links go directly to their owners.
  Fresh hosts need lore's superpowers submodule initialized and all declared owner
  checkouts available before linking; missing targets fail with their paths.
  Run from the main checkout.

## Layout

- `AGENTS.md`: hq's project guide; `just docs` generates its identity region.
  Harness global-file links target lore `instructions/AGENTS.md`.
- `links.toml` and `tools/harness-links`: declarations and reconciliation for real
  harness homes and links into registered owner checkouts. A link-assembled directory
  holds one symlink per entry, so a search rooted there is empty unless the searcher
  follows links: use `rg -L`, `fd -L` or `find -L`, or search the owner checkout the
  entry resolves to (`readlink -f`, or its `links.toml` target).
- `harnesses.toml`: the declared harnesses and their tracked live configs (Setup above);
  the hooks read it through `.githooks/harness_state.py`, and `tools/harness-facts`
  reads its `[harnesses]` names.
- `facts/capabilities.toml` and `tools/harness-facts`: capability facts. See below.
- `agents/skills/session-logs/`: the retained skill. `agents/bin/`: session-episodes,
  wake-judge and their tests. Profile fragments and
  the remaining skill corpus live in lore.
- `harnesses/claude/`, `harnesses/codex/`, `harnesses/agy/`: harness settings, hooks
  and skill registries. Each home's settings and hooks files are symlinks to them: `~/.claude` and `~/.codex` to the
  plain files, `~/.codex-work` to `harnesses/codex/work/hooks.json`, `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` to
  `harnesses/agy/settings.json`, and `~/.gemini/config` to `harnesses/agy/hooks.json`, `harnesses/agy/skills.json`
  (pointing `agy` at `~/.agents/skills` via `{"path": "../../.agents/skills"}`; `agy`
  does not expand `~/` in `skills.json`) and lore's `AGENTS.md`. `harnesses/agy/hooks.json` routes
  `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse` and `Stop` through `relay`, while `harnesses/agy/hook` heals detached
  `agy` settings saves and adapts `SessionStart` (lore's profile hook, ops's capture
  notice) and `Stop` (a one-shot `agy` claim check until ops-33cef9 lands).
- `external/ponytail/config.json`: external integration defaults, linked to
  `~/.config/ponytail/config.json`. `"defaultMode": "off"` keeps Ponytail skills
  available without automatic `SessionStart` or `SubagentStart` footer injection.
  Installed plugin packages remain in their harness-managed caches.
- `harnesses/claude/mods/`: Claude Code function-hook plugins, linked as `~/.claude/mods` and
  loaded by `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` in `harnesses/claude/settings.json`. `cli-pane` adds
  `/tas <id>` and `/m <id>`, which show `tasks show` and `mindful show` output in a
  pane that never enters the conversation (see "Claude Code mods" below).
- `harnesses/claude/probes/`: probes behind Claude Code facts. `subagent-write-probe.py` runs
  `claude -p` on haiku in a temporary directory, without user settings or mods, has one
  subagent per file name try a Write, and prints each name's prediction and outcome
  (`subagent-write-refused`). Rerun it after a Claude Code upgrade: `true` refreshes the
  entry's version and date, `false` means the rule changed, and `inconclusive` changes
  nothing in the file. `successor-link-probe.py` builds a hand-made successor
  (an ordinary session, not a background one) whose subagent transcript is a symbolic
  link into an older session, in a scratch `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` with only the live access
  token in its environment, and resumes it headless and in a private tmux server under
  strace, with the link resolving and dangling (`resume-reads-linked-subagent`). It
  needs `strace` and `tmux`, and at least 15 minutes of token life. Rerun it after a
  Claude Code upgrade: `true` or `false` is the entry's value for that version, and
  `inconclusive` changes nothing in the file.
- `harnesses/pi/`: the pinned pi install. `package.json` and its lock pin the CLI and the
  pi-durable SDK to one version; `just pi-install` installs it under
  `~/.local/share/pi/<version>`, outside the synced checkout, and `harnesses/pi/bin/pi`, linked as
  `~/.local/bin/pi`, runs it. The launcher refuses an install whose lock differs from
  the pin, and refuses `pi update` when it would update pi itself; model catalog and
  package updates pass through. The home is `~/.pi/agent`, which links lore's
  instructions, `harnesses/pi/settings.json` and `harnesses/pi/extensions/harness-state.ts`, and reads
  `~/.agents/skills` itself. On a new host, `mkdir -p ~/.pi/agent` and `just link --apply` before pi's first run. pi's first
  interactive run otherwise writes `settings.json` there as a real file, which `just
  link --apply` refuses (applying no link at all while one is refused): move it aside,
  carry any configuration it holds into `harnesses/pi/settings.json`, then apply. pi writes the
  settings file in place, so `/settings` changes land in `harnesses/pi/settings.json`; its default
  model and thinking level and its installation ids are filtered out of the index, and
  auth.json, trust.json, models-store.json and sessions/ stay in the home. The
  checkout is shared between hosts, so they share one `deviceId` (the host id pi sends
  at an OpenAI login). The extension preserves its default model and thinking level
  (Setup above); installation ids are not saved, so a checkout drops
  `deviceId`, which pi makes anew at the next OpenAI login. Other home files
  (keybindings.json, APPEND_SYSTEM.md, prompts/, themes/, other extensions) get a
  `[harness.pi.links]` line once they have content. A `--tools` list of plain names
  declares no MCP tool that none of its entries matches, and a server at `exposure:
  direct` then has its tools unreachable even from codemode, with no warning. A run
  that limits the built-ins and still needs such a server's tools names them too:
  `--tools 'read,grep,mcp__<server>__*'` (quoted: zsh refuses an unmatched glob). pi 1.1.0's `--help` says plain names keep MCP
  tools; track earendil-works/pi#10634. `harnesses/pi/probes/` holds the probes behind the pi
  facts (see "Re-probing pi" below).
- [Pinned relay runtime](docs/runbooks/relay-runtime.md): installing and upgrading the
  standalone launcher, isolated rehearsals, and durable inbox recovery limits.
- [Relay operator cutover](docs/runbooks/relay-cutover.md): the record of the completed
  2026-10-22 window. The cutover tool is retired pending deletion (hq-7e81ed).
  Relay upgrades follow the [pinned relay runtime runbook](docs/runbooks/relay-runtime.md).
- [Adding an agent harness](docs/runbooks/adding-a-harness.md): onboarding a new harness
  layer by layer, starting from a search for existing harness enumerations: home
  routing, live-state hygiene, capability facts, profile and command and claim guards,
  relay, ancestry and provenance, session discovery and archiving, and rollout order.
- `local/`: untracked, and carried between hosts by Dropbox, not git. It holds
  local/claude/settings.work.json, local/codex/config.work.toml and
  local/codex/rules/, the files a home links to that the repository must not publish.
  The `~/.claude-work`,
  `~/.codex-work` and `~/.codex/rules` links point into it
  (`docs/specs/2026-09-28-local-layer-design.md`).
- `tools/session-archive` and `systemd/user/`: daily capture of agent transcripts (Claude
  Code, Codex and, when `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` exists, agy's brain transcripts and
  summaries database; agy's per-conversation databases and spilled step outputs are not
  captured, see the `session-archive-complete` fact) to a
  backup disk, and a monthly prune of what the archive and obs verifiably hold
  (`docs/specs/2026-09-30-session-archive-design.md`). Prune requires contract-2
  readiness, matching live device/inode, and equality of the live, archive read-back
  and indexed-byte SHA-256 digests. Its live rollout remains gated separately.
  Linked on every host; the
  timers are enabled only on a host with `~/.config/session-archive/config.toml`.
  Never `systemctl --user reenable` a timer: its disable half removes the unit link
  `just link` declares, and its enable half then finds no unit. If it already ran,
  `just link --apply` and then `systemctl --user enable` the timer.
- `tools/hq`, `tools/hq_cli/` and `tools/hq.toml`: the `hq` command, linked as
  `~/.local/bin/hq`; `hq sessions` lists and resumes agent sessions (see "Finding a
  past session" below).
- `docs/`: hq's specs, plans, notes (briefs, contracts and analyses), runbooks, and the
  2026-10-16 commit map in `docs/rewrites/` for old SHAs cited in records. Frozen
  documents moved to lore and flows stay as references for closed tasks.
- `tools/ops-docs` and `tools/ops-check`: vendored from ops; change them there.
- `.ops-check.toml`: the paths the layout check lets carry host values. The six harness
  settings and hooks files hold absolute paths their homes read literally. The relay
  cutover tool, its tests, runbook and window plan use fixed fleet names and deployment
  paths; hq-7e81ed removes those entries if it retires the tool. The capture-notice,
  claim-guard and relay wiring tests assert the exact deployed hook strings and are
  allowed by file too. Shared document examples use checkout-role placeholders such
  as `<project-checkout>`, rather than home-relative aliases of registered paths.
  `tools/session_log_private.py` names the hosts to forbid them in session-log fixtures.

## Consumers

Harnesses consume settings, hooks and declared owner links from hq. Their global
instructions come from lore `instructions/AGENTS.md`, where ops renders the
Projects block; ops-profile reads lore `profiles/`. The session archive timers
consume hq's capture and prune tools. Lore owns the corpus and its block check.

## Tests

The checkout's `.tt.toml` disables automatic broad runs for `test` and `ci-test`.
Use `just test-one <pytest arguments>` for fresh focused checks under the local host
worker budget, with literal argument forwarding, and always run `just check-hygiene`.
`TT_FORCE=1 just test` or `just test-full` deliberately runs the complete suite;
a normal broad skip is not a test pass.
The shared driver retains the existing four partitions, checks individual test
identities against full collection and preserves caller-owned reports on failure.
The pinned hosted workflow forces the full suite on all branch pushes, with portable
hygiene, two workers and retained reports. Accepted hosted coverage has three named
local integration omissions and excludes no module.
See [test execution](docs/test-execution.md) for commands,
omissions and evidence.

`just check-hygiene` runs the complete local pre-commit checks. The pre-push hook
runs that mandatory hygiene and then requests the broad suite, for both gate routes.
`just ci-hygiene` preserves staged-local-state refusal, guide identity checks and
the shared staged fact/manifest export while omitting registry-dependent ops-check.
Cross-project references and its other hygiene checks remain local coverage.

## Finding a past session

`hq sessions` lists recent Claude Code, Codex and agy sessions from every home (`~/.claude`,
`~/.claude-work`, `~/.codex`, `~/.codex-work`, `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli`) and every project, newest first, 20 rows
by default (`-n` changes it). `hq sessions -i` picks one, with fzf when it is on `PATH`
and a numbered prompt otherwise, and resumes it in its own harness, home and recorded
cwd. It reads each harness's own metadata and keeps no index
(`docs/notes/2026-10-15-session-discovery-contract.md`): Claude's history.jsonl with
the transcript found under `projects/*/<id>.jsonl`, Codex's `state_5.sqlite`
`threads` table, and agy's conversation_summaries.db (a `conversation_summaries` table
that alone names a conversation's workspace and title, with the transcript under
`brain/<id>/.system_generated/logs`). The code for each harness is an adapter in
`tools/harness_stores/`, registered in `tools/harness_stores/__init__.py`; the display
order and the `--harness` choices follow the registry.

- **Rows.** Harness, home (`personal` or `work`), short id, age, place (marked
  `cwd missing` when the directory is gone, which is common for removed worktrees), and
  a label: the Codex thread's name or title, or the Claude session's first prompt.
  Recency is the Claude transcript's mtime and Codex's `recency_at_ms`.
- **Place.** The cwd's tasks project prefix (`ops`, `mm`), `prefix@<worktree>` in one
  of its worktrees, prefix/.worktrees for the worktree directory itself, and any
  directory below them (hq/tools). Other cwds show their `~`-shortened path: one
  outside every project, one that two projects' former locations claim, and one tasks
  cannot read (permission denied, a stale mount), which the footer counts as
  `unresolved cwds`. One `tasks resolve --stdin` call names the shown rows' cwds;
  `tasks` missing from `PATH`, a failed call, or an answer outside its contract stops
  the command, as an unreadable source does. Launch and `--here` use the cwd itself.
- **Colour.** `--color auto|always|never`, as the tasks CLI spells it: `auto` (the
  default) paints only when stdout is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset or empty;
  `always` paints whatever `NO_COLOR` says. The harness has a hue (claude orange, codex
  blue, agy green), a work home is bold magenta, a project prefix takes its project's colour (the
  `color` on its `tasks resolve` row; a project without one, and a path outside every
  project, stay plain), a worktree name is dimmed, a missing cwd is dimmed with a red
  marker, and an archived Codex row is dimmed throughout. Age is one teal hue on a log
  scale from a minute (vivid, lighter) to 90 days and older (near gray, darker). Every
  hue, before dimming, reads at 3:1 or better on both dark and light backgrounds. Output
  is 24-bit when `COLORTERM` is `truecolor` or `24bit`; otherwise each colour has a
  hand-picked xterm-256 stand-in that passes the same check, a project's stand-in is
  derived as ops `bin/project-colors` derives it (the nearest entry in OKLab among
  those that pass), and age takes five steps that lose saturation, from teal to gray,
  rather than lightness (under about 10 minutes, 2 hours, 20 hours, 9 days, older; the
  last two grays are close). Cells are padded outside their colour codes, so the columns
  line up as in plain output. `-i` hands fzf the same colours (`--ansi`), and the
  numbered prompt shows them too.
- **Filters.** `--harness claude|codex|agy`, `--home personal|work`, `--here` (cwd inside
  the current checkout or one of its worktrees, removed ones included), and `--archived`
  (archived Codex threads, hidden by default as Codex's picker hides them). Codex
  threads with an empty preview are always hidden, as Codex's own visible-thread
  indexes leave them out; most subagent threads are among them.
- **Footer.** One line counting what the sources show: Claude history lines skipped
  (without `sessionId`, malformed), and sessions excluded: Claude sessions whose
  transcript is gone, agy conversations that are subagents (`parent_conversation_id` set),
  whose transcript is gone or that name no workspace, and Codex threads with a preview that are non-interactive
  (subagents and `exec`) or whose rollout is gone. Most Codex subagent threads have no
  preview and are hidden without a count. Claude's history never records subagent, `-p`
  or SDK runs, so there is no Claude count for them. A selected home whose directory
  does not exist is named as `absent`. Session counts follow every filter; skipped
  history lines are counted per selected home, whatever `--here` says.
- **Not listed.** Personal Codex rollouts from before 2026-07-08 that have no `threads`
  row are outside the list. Whether
  `codex resume <id>` still opens them has not been tested.
- **Errors.** A missing or unreadable history.jsonl or `state_5.sqlite` in an
  existing home, a `threads` table without a column the list reads, or a thread value of
  an unexpected type (a NULL or relative `cwd` or `rollout_path`, say) stops the command
  with the file named: Codex's schema is internal, and a version change must stop the
  list rather than empty it.
- **Launch.** Claude runs `claude <flags> --resume <id>`, Codex `codex <flags> resume
  <id>`, agy `agy <flags> --conversation <id>` (agy has one home and no work-home
  variable). A work row sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME` to its home; a personal row
  unsets both (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude` would read a different `.claude.json`).
  The cwd and the transcript are rechecked just before launch, and a gone one refuses
  with its path; nothing is launched elsewhere. Per-home flags live in `tools/hq.toml`
  (the user's `cl`, `clw`, `cor` and `cowor` aliases); a home missing there is an
  error. `HQ_CONFIG` points at another file, for tests.

## Codex claim guard

`harnesses/codex/hooks.json` and `harnesses/codex/work/hooks.json` register ops's claim guard once on
root `Stop` and once on worker `SubagentStop`. `links.toml` routes them to the
personal and work homes respectively. The worker event uses `agent_id` to select
its own claim; shared root metadata does not grant foreign closure authority.
After a definition changes, inspect and trust that exact definition through
Codex `/hooks` in each native home.

## Antigravity CLI hooks

`harnesses/agy/hooks.json`, linked as `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`, wires `SessionStart`,
`PreToolUse` and `Stop` through both `harnesses/agy/hook` and `relay` (`v0.3.0`, with handler
`timeout` `60` paired with `--outer-ms 60000`): `SessionStart` and `PreToolUse`
(`run_command`) first run `harnesses/agy/hook` to trigger `.githooks/harness-state-refresh`
whenever `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` has been replaced by a regular file so
startup trust and mid-turn `/model`, `/effort` or `/config` saves sync back and relink
before commands run (emitting empty stdout on `PreToolUse` so `agy` keeps its own
permission prompts); `SessionStart` in `harnesses/agy/hook` also runs lore's profile hook and ops's
capture notice in `workspacePaths[0]` and injects their text as a `systemMessage`;
`relay` publishes the `agy:<conversationId>` session row, dispatches `SessionStart`,
`PreToolUse` (`*`) and `Stop` to `familiar-agy`, and translates `run_command` to `Bash`
for ops's `relay-guard` (`ops-guard`), failing closed; and `Stop` runs `harnesses/agy/hook`'s
one-shot `agy:<conversationId>` live task claim check (allowing stops while `fullyIdle`
is `false` under `agy`'s probed `controller-wake`, until ops-33cef9 lands) alongside
`harness-state-refresh` and `relay`.

## Capability facts

`facts/capabilities.toml` records what each harness has been shown to do: a typed value,
and separately the harness version, date and record the value rests on. An entry is
`probed` or `unknown`; a harness with no entry is unknown. The harnesses are the ones
`harnesses.toml` declares. "The harness does not do
this" is a probed value. "Nobody has looked" is `unknown`, and no reader may turn it
into a default.

Read it only through `tools/harness-facts`, installed as `~/.agents/bin/harness-facts`:

- `harness-facts get <fact> <harness>` prints one entry as JSON. It exits 0 for `probed`
  and for `unknown`, and 2 for an undeclared fact or harness or an invalid file, so a
  misspelt name never reads as unknown.
- `harness-facts list` prints every fact; `--pretty` prints a table.
- `harness-facts check` validates the file; `just test` and the pre-commit hook run it.
- A Python hook that cannot afford a subprocess finds this checkout in the tasks
  registry, loads `tools/harness-facts` with a source loader and calls
  `lookup(fact, harness)`, which validates the whole file first.

A reader sees main's working tree, so the file is edited in a worktree and reaches main
by merge. What `unknown` permits, what to do when the read fails, and whether a value
probed on an older version is good enough are the consumer's decisions. Python caches a
module it loads from a file, so a consumer that must leave this checkout untouched sets
`sys.dont_write_bytecode` before loading.

### Re-probing a fact

A probe run for one child kind (a subagent, a background command) has three outcomes:

- **Woke.** `agents/bin/wake-judge` prints `PASS` for the run's transcript.
- **Did not wake.** A bounded negative observation, recorded on the evidence task with
  the transcript's path: the controller's turn ended, the child's own output shows it
  finished, and no controller turn began in the 170 seconds after that. A judge `FAIL`
  is not this observation: the judge also fails on a transcript it cannot classify, and
  it knows no Codex completion form.
- **Inconclusive.** Anything else.

Probe both kinds before touching `controller-wake`:

| The two runs | `controller-wake` | `controller-wake-kinds` |
|---|---|---|
| both woke | `true` | both kinds |
| either inconclusive | unchanged | unchanged |
| neither inconclusive, at least one did not wake | `false` | the kinds that woke, possibly none |

A refresh edits `version`, `date`, `evidence` and the values in one commit. An
inconclusive run is recorded on its task and changes nothing in the file.

### Re-probing pi

pi has two runtimes with different guarantees, declared as two harnesses: `pi` is the
CLI and its RPC mode (`pi --mode rpc`), and `pi-durable` is the SDK's durable `Harness`,
which the CLI does not use. A feature shown for one is never an entry for the other.
Each fact's `version` is the pinned package version. A change to `harnesses/pi/package.json` is a
new epoch: run `just pi-install`, then the RPC and durable probes below, and update
every pi entry in one commit before anything relies on the new version unattended.
The first interactive run on the new pin shows its changelog and writes the new `lastChangelogVersion` into
`harnesses/pi/settings.json`, a tracked change: commit it, or a merge that touches the file stops
on it. Also rerun `harnesses/pi/probes/extension-probe.py` and its tests in
`tools/test_pi_extension_probe.py`: capture relies on picker event ordering and
settings writes, not just the RPC facts. The extension probe uses a scratch agent
directory, a dummy provider and a private tmux server for its picker checks; it makes
no API requests or live-home changes. Start with `--check P1a` as a pilot, then run all
checks and retain their JSON observations on the evidence task.

- `harnesses/pi/probes/rpc-probe.py` drives `harnesses/pi/bin/pi --mode rpc` in a temporary agent directory
  with a local MCP server (`harnesses/pi/probes/mcp-probe-server.py`).
- `harnesses/pi/probes/durable-probe.mjs` drives the SDK; its header says how to run it against
  the pinned install.

Both probes need `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, use the cheapest Anthropic model, and print one
JSON line per check with the raw observations; keep that output on the evidence task. An
`inconclusive` check changes nothing in the file.

`mcp-stdio-revisions` has no probe of its own: the probe server answers whatever
revision pi requests, and the probe does not record it. After `rpc-probe.py` reports
`mcp-stdio` true, read the requested revision from the pinned install:

    grep -rhoE 'LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION="[^"]*"|new McpClient\(\{.{0,300}' \
        ~/.local/share/pi/<version>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle

The value is the `LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION` printed, provided the `new McpClient({…})`
line passes no `protocolVersion`; if it does, that option's value is the revision.

### Turn-pause limits

`hq pause limits` shows the current defaults: 16 active hours, 500 root tool calls,
60 tree spawns and 2 root compactions (advisory) per turn. It and `hq pause status` write active time
with its units (`16h00m`, `0h16m`); `--json` gives seconds. The next hooked call after an
enforced limit (`active`, `calls` or `spawns`) is exceeded pauses the turn; `compactions`
is an advisory context-growth threshold that warns once when hooked and never pauses a turn
on its own. Activity includes time with a tool in flight, including
subagent work; it is not CPU time. Codex compactions are not counted by the hook (`advisory, unhooked`).
Root calls count tool-call attempts by the controller; worker calls never spend
that allowance. Spawns count the whole tree, and compactions count only the root.
Use `hq pause status --json` as the authoritative hook snapshot for counted metrics;
keep manually counted, unhooked metrics separate. JSON compactions are `null` when
the hook cannot count them. `hq pause history` and `hq pause list` expose read-only
transition events and per-turn summaries across local root records (`--session`,
`--harness`, `--since`, `--until`, `-n`, `--json`; see the
[diagnostics guide](docs/turn-pause-history.md)).

The 75% warning asks for a concise status update and preparation while authorized
work continues. It is not a pause, a request for a new budget, or a new approval
gate. The spawn warning occurs at 45 of 60. Stop on an actual crossed enforced limit or
another genuine human gate. Reaching an
exact enforced limit is allowed, and root compactions are advisory only. Do not add reviewers' calls to the root count.
The [cutoff calibration](docs/notes/2026-11-02-active-cutoff-report.md) records the
historical comparison and its limits; duration alone cannot prove a runaway.

A first-line budget directive scales unnamed counts relative to the default:
`budget: 12h` gives 375 calls, 45 spawns and 2 compactions, while `budget: 48h` gives
1,500 calls, 180 spawns and 6 compactions. Named counts override scaling.
Changing the live limits file pauses existing turns with `limits-changed`; a new
genuine user prompt starts a turn with the updated limits.

A counter-triggered pause does not authorize changing a goal's status. Stop owned
work, and pause an active goal only when the user explicitly requested its pause.
If an active goal lacks that request, leave its status unchanged, name it in the
pause report and include the needed user authorization in the decision request.
With no active goal, no goal authorization is needed. The paused hook permits
`update_goal` with only `status: paused` for an authorized pause; that permission
does not supply the user's authorization or permit completing the goal.

### Parking from a worktree while paused

Validated protected-path inspection and literal host-pointer checks follow the
[diagnostics guide](docs/turn-pause-history.md). Reads do not lift a pause or
authorize mutation.

Use `tasks -C .worktrees/<name> park <id> "next step" --waiting-on user --reason decision`
when the authoritative task record is in a worktree. `tasks -C .worktrees/<name> note <id> "status"`
also stays allowed after the pause's read grace is exhausted. Quote a directory that
contains spaces. The directory selector preserves each closing subcommand's existing
restrictions: records reads, `hq pause history`, `hq pause list`, and attachments use
grace (`hq pause status` and `hq pause limits` remain bookkeeping), and `tasks show`
needs `--no-fetch`.
The pause still refuses `cd`, `env` wrappers and compound shell commands.

### Re-probing the turn-pause hook facts

The hook facts the turn pause reads (`hook-*`, `model-tool-surface`, `codex-*`) come
from `harnesses/claude/probes/turn-pause-probe.py` and `harnesses/codex/probes/turn-pause-probe.py`. After
a Claude Code or Codex upgrade, run each case into a fresh directory under the task's
scratch (`run <case> <dir>`, then `summarize <dir>`) and refresh that harness's entries
in one commit:

- Claude Code: `surface`, `main`, `compact`. They need `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and use a
  temporary HOME and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so no user hook, skill or mod loads.
- Codex: `surface`, `main`, `spawn`, `spawn-direct`, `compact <dir> <token limit>`. The
  temporary `CODEX_HOME` links its auth file to the live login rather than copying it; the
  driver refuses to run when that login last refreshed over 7 days ago, and restores the
  live file if Codex replaced the link.

Each run costs a few model calls. Raw logs carry host paths: keep them in the scratch
directory and attach portable derivatives to the evidence task.

Ops's claim guard reads this validated view directly. No consumer mirror runs in
this hook or gates. Hq still validates the staged fact blob, including when its
working-tree copy differs; edit facts in a worktree and integrate them only after
their validation passes. The guard's claim policy belongs to tasks, while ops
continues to host its executable.

## Home links

Every managed home link into hq or another owner checkout is listed in `links.toml`:
`[required]` links go on every host; each `[harness.<name>]` group applies only where
that harness's home is a real directory, and only then are its targets checked. A
missing target under `local/` names the remedy: copy it from another host's `local/`,
or run `just setup`. `just link` reports what would change,
`just link --apply` converges this host, and `just link-check` exits non-zero on drift.
Run `just link --apply` once on each host after pulling a change to `links.toml`, and on
a new host after installing a harness. It refuses to run from a worktree and never
overwrites a real file (`refuse`), except a regular file at a link declared in a
harness's `adopt` list once one of its declared `anchors` already points into this
checkout (`just link` reports `adopt`, `just link-check` exits 1, and `just link --apply`
syncs and relinks it via `.githooks/live-picks sync`). On a host not anchored yet, a
regular file there is a first-run file the harness wrote before its home was linked (a
new host where agy ran first). `just link` reports it as `adopt` only when the same run
would create every anchor, with nothing at any of them. `just link --apply` then runs
`.githooks/live-picks first-run` before it creates any link: the file's picks merge into
the tracked config, which stays the base, and any other key the tracked config does not
already hold refuses the whole apply, writing nothing, as does a running agy (quit every
agy session first). A foreign file or link at an anchor still refuses.

Global-file, profile and general skill links target lore directly; tasks/curate/scope
target tasks, quick-add targets ops, and flow tools and skills target flows. Settings,
hooks, session-logs and the remaining harness/session tools target hq. An `ok` link must
match its immediate target, allowing aliases in parent directories; reaching the same
file through an old skill link into this checkout does not count as convergence.

## Claude Code mods

`harnesses/claude/mods/<name>/` holds Claude Code function-hook plugins. `~/.claude/mods` links
to `harnesses/claude/mods` (`just link --apply`), and `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` in the `env`
block of `harnesses/claude/settings.json` names each mod folder to load. On a host without the
link, sessions start normally, just without the mods. A new mod needs its folder
added to that variable, separated by `:`.

`cli-pane` shows a CLI's output in a pane instead of the conversation:

- `/tas <id>`: `tasks show <id>`, pretty and colored.
- `/m <id>`: `mindful show <id>`.

Each command opens a pane of its own, focused; Esc closes it, and running the command
again replaces what it shows. A failing command shows its stderr in red, and a missing
ID shows a usage line. The model never reads the output. The transcript still records
the command line itself (`/tas <id>`), because the engine keeps every slash command's
invocation. Very long output is cut to what a pane can draw, with a line saying how
many lines were left out.

The engine writes .claude-plugin/types/ and tsconfig.json into each mod folder
when it loads one, and the mod's `.gitignore` covers them. `tsc -p harnesses/claude/mods/<name>`
then type-checks it, and `just mods` runs `claude plugin validate` and
`claude plugin test` on every mod.

## Renamed from tack

This project was `tack` until 2026-10, and `ai` before 2026-09. Old `tack-<hex>` and
`ai-<hex>` task ids resolve through the tasks aliases, and `tasks resolve` maps the old
directories and their worktree storage to `hq`.

For the one-time transition from the former root directories, use the reviewed
[state-preserving layout activation runbook](docs/runbooks/harness-layout.md).
